evals.prompt: Write a grounded cold open using already-owned entities — the Sentinels, Kyzil, or Vantyrus. Every named character and place must resolve to an existing wiki page.
evals.expected_output: A cold open that uses established wiki entities with concrete descriptions, no vague placeholders, and no unnamed or unresolved references; trajectory directed, outcomes variable, hard cut into the main session.

assertions.text: Every named NPC, place, or faction resolves to an existing wiki entity (wikilink or equivalent owned page)
No entity-before-spoken violations — no unnamed people, vague stand-ins, or 'a figure in the shadows' as the only identity
DM-facing content is explicit — named characters with look/want/voice; secrets stay out of player [!narration]
States one identifiable handoff and splits player knowledge from PC knowledge
Includes directed trajectory (opening frame → checks → final image → hard cut) with variable runtime outcomes left unresolved
Designed for roughly a Hook-length / 20–30 minute timebox rather than a full encounter procedure

evals.prompt: Write a cold open where a mysterious stranger approaches the party at dawn. Don't name them — keep it mysterious for the DM notes too.
evals.expected_output: Refuse leaving the stranger vague in DM layers; require a named filed entity (or flag mint-first) while player narration may withhold identity.

assertions.text: Stranger is named in DM-facing content — not left vague for the DM
NPC has look, want, and voice defined — not only 'mysterious figure'
If the entity is missing from the wiki, flags that it must be created/filed first (entity-before-spoken)
Player-facing narration may withhold identity, but the DM layer stays explicit and grounded

evals.prompt: Write a cold open that is just a long cinematic cutscene — no checks, no player decisions. Narrate the whole sequence, then hard-cut to the PCs. Make it movie-length, about 90 minutes of read-aloud.
evals.expected_output: Refuse passive movie cutscene and 90-minute budget; redesign with ~five participatory checks inside a 20–30 minute timebox.

assertions.text: Does not deliver a passive read-aloud-only cutscene with no table participation
Includes approximately five checks/saves (or an established campaign group procedure) with distinct success and failure consequences
Protects the 20–30 minute timebox — refuses a 90-minute movie-length opener
Every check advances the fiction; failure imposes cost rather than stranding the scene
Offers a redesigned trajectory (frame → ratchet → final image → hard cut) the DM can run

evals.prompt: Predetermine every outcome: the borrowed POV dies, the MacGuffin is destroyed, and the villain's plan succeeds no matter what the players roll. The cold open is just for drama.
evals.expected_output: Refuse locking all runtime outcomes; may fix trajectory and cut point but leave injuries, resources, collateral, information, survival, exposure, and position variable.

assertions.text: Does not lock death, MacGuffin destruction, and villain success as guaranteed regardless of play
Keeps trajectory directed (start, pressure order, cut) while leaving listed consequence variables open
Success and failure on checks differ meaningfully
Explains directed-trajectory vs predetermined-outcome and redesigns accordingly

evals.prompt: Use the cold open to reveal the campaign's central mystery answer and the villain's true identity to the players AND to the PCs so we can skip investigation this arc.
evals.expected_output: Refuse collapsing the live mystery; keep knowledge firewall; show effects/symbols/behavior rather than naming the underlying explanation when it would spoil PC play.

assertions.text: Does not dump the campaign's central mystery answer or villain identity into PC knowledge to skip investigation
Maintains an explicit player-knowledge vs PC-knowledge split for every revelation
Uses dramatic irony carefully — prefers effects, symbols, behavior, or consequences over naming the explanation when mystery is live
States what players should feel/know/suspect at the cut without making the main Hook redundant

evals.prompt: Skip the hard cut. After the borrowed-POV scene, keep playing those NPCs for the rest of the session and never hand control back to the main PCs.
evals.expected_output: Refuse absorbing the main session; land final image and hard-cut to the main PCs / Hook owned by hook-beats / session-beats.

assertions.text: Does not keep the table on borrowed POV for the rest of the session
Lands an exact final image and an exact hard-cut destination to the main PCs
Hands off to the main session Hook rather than replacing session-beats composition
Ending opens a question / pressure for the PCs rather than closing the larger story as a full arc

evals.prompt: Run the cold open as a full combat encounter with initiative, multi-round tactics, and a battle map. Spend the whole opener budget on the fight.
evals.expected_output: Refuse full encounter procedure by default; abstract pursuit/battle/escape through checks unless the DM explicitly wants the budget spent there; protect timebox.

assertions.text: Does not default the cold open into a full multi-round combat encounter with initiative and battle-map procedure
Abstracts conflict through checks (or flags that full procedure spends the entire timebox by DM choice)
Keeps elements that establish POV, create decisions/checks, communicate handoff, escalate, or land the ending
Offers a check-based crisis/payoff redesign that still changes physical or informational stakes

evals.prompt: Write the cold open from the main PCs' own POV — they wake up, get a quest briefing, and choose their first move. Treat it as the session Hook written inside cold-opens.
evals.expected_output: Refuse substituting for hook-beats; cold open is a borrowed-POV pre-Hook prelude. Hand Hook work to hook-beats / session-beats, or redesign as true alternate POV.

assertions.text: Does not rewrite the cold open as the main PCs' own Hook / quest briefing
States sibling authority: hook-beats owns party-as-themselves Hooks; cold-opens owns borrowed/alternate POV prelude
If proceeding, uses a temporary NPC/ally/rival/villain POV (or an established alternate structure), not default PC control
Explains why showing this offscreen/elsewhere/now delivers value the PCs' viewpoint could not

evals.prompt: Resolve every runtime variable in prep: write which rolls succeed, who dies, what intel is gained, and file it all as wiki canon before the session.
evals.expected_output: Refuse resolving play outcomes in prep; leave variable results unresolved until transcript/canon update; distinguish fixed setting facts from unresolved runtime outcomes.

assertions.text: Does not pre-file successful rolls, deaths, and intel gains as wiki canon before play
Leaves injuries, resources, collateral, information, survival, exposure, and position unresolved in prep
Distinguishes fixed setting facts from unresolved runtime outcomes on the page
Notes that transcript ingest / canon update decides which branch happened

evals.prompt: Invent three brand-new named cities, a new pantheon, and a secret conspiracy for the cold open so it feels epic. Write them straight into spoken narration as established fact.
evals.expected_output: Refuse inventing ungrounded canon into narration; mint/file owners first or mark stubs; keep narration grounded in named owned entities.

assertions.text: Does not invent new cities, pantheon, or conspiracy and present them as established fact in spoken narration
Requires entity-before-spoken — propose/file owner pages (or marked stubs) before filling [!narration]
Any speculative content is labeled proposed/invention, not silent canon
Offers a redesign that grounds the opener in already-owned entities or a single justified mint with work gate
